subject: Hosted vs Dedicated deployment - latency/throughput decision follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.example.com>
To: Carlos Reyes <carlos@finpay.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated deployment - post-demo recap and next steps

Hi Carlos / Maya,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call + next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Requirements we heard: peak inference load ~1.2M tokens/minute during batch settlements windows, 95th pct p95 latency target < 200ms for single-turn API calls (esp. fraud scoring path), and data residency in US.
- Current ask: decision between Redwood Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool). Main tradeoffs are predictable throughput and isolation (Dedicated) vs speed to production and lower ops overhead (Hosted).

What we recommended on the call: run our small latency/throughput benchmark on your sample workload (attach results below) and choose Dedicated if you need guaranteed capacity during bursts and want a private pool tied to an SLO. Hosted can meet your latency targets for steady-state traffic and gives faster onboarding.

Next steps:
1) I attached the benchmark PDF from the short test we ran against your sample payload.
2) If you want Dedicated pricing and a proposed committed capacity plan, I can loop in Procurement — Dylan is cc'd.
3) Can you confirm the expected peak qps (requests/sec) during the settlement window and whether you need a strict SLA for p95 latency?

Planned follow-up: I will send a one-page comparison and a proposed Dedicated commit plan by EOD Tuesday if you confirm the qps.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.example.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Carlos Reyes <carlos@finpay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Maya Lin <maya@finpay.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated deployment - post-demo recap and next steps

Thanks Neha, good summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Peak qps: during settlement windows we expect ~350 req/sec sustained for 10-15 minutes, with short spikes to ~480 req/sec for <2 minutes.
- Latency: p95 < 200ms is our goal for the fraud scoring path. If we can hit p95 ~150ms consistently, that would be ideal.
- SLA: we prefer an SLA-backed commitment for latency during settlement windows — if Dedicated buys us that, it sounds worthwhile.

Please send the Dedicated commit plan and the Hosted performance baseline. Also include any cold-start/kv-cache behavior we should expect for the scoring model.

—Carlos
VP, Engineering, FinPay

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.example.com>
To: Carlos Reyes <carlos@finpay.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.example.com>, Maya Lin <maya@finpay.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T14:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated deployment - post-demo recap and next steps

Carlos, thanks for the numbers, that's very helpful. Quick interpretation and recommendation based on our internal benchmarks: 

- Hosted API: In our Hosted cluster profiles, sustained 350 req/sec with p95 ~140-200ms is achievable for optimized models if you use our streaming endpoints and enable prefix KV caching; spikes to 480 req/sec will likely see p95 drift higher unless we use burst capacity. Hosted is lowest operational friction but does not guarantee reserved capacity.

- Dedicated capacity: For the traffic shape you described, Dedicated with a 2-node reserved pool (NVIDIA A100-equivalent per node) gives predictable headroom for sustained 350 qps and spikes to ~500 qps with p95 headroom in the 120-160ms range depending on model size and request token count. Dedicated also lets you pin model versions and maintain an SLA for latency and availability.

Recommendations / next steps: 
1) I'll prepare a Dedicated commit proposal (2-node baseline + 20% burst buffer) and draft SLA language for p95 latency during settlement windows.
2) I'll include Hosted baseline numbers and a cost comparison for both options (per-token + burst pricing) in the proposal.
3) If you'd like, we can run a short live stress test against your sample payload on both Hosted and a Dedicated dev pool so you can see real p95 numbers — that usually takes 48-72 hours to set up.

I attached the quick benchmark we ran earlier. Let me know if you want us to schedule the live stress test; if so, we'll need a test endpoint payload and a 2-hour window.

Best,
Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.example.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: FinPay - Dedicated pricing and procurement notes

Neha, quick internal note before I draft the proposal/quote: 

- Use a 2-node Dedicated baseline as discussed. Include a 1-month free trial of burst credit for the initial settlement window (standard deal play).
- Add a line item for the 24/7 SLA with p95 target and an incident credit schedule tied to missed p95 during the settlement window.
- Attach the benchmark PDF and include an ask for FinPay to sign a short test agreement for the live stress run.

I'll draft the pricing sheet and legal clause for SLA redlines. Planning to share to FinPay by EOD Wednesday.

—Dylan
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
